entrypoints.summary: The minimized syzkaller program creates a Bluetooth SCO socket and issues an asynchronous SCO connect followed by another SCO connect.
The supplied C reproducer is the executable form of the SCO socket and connection-lifecycle trigger.

affected_components.role: Timeout and connection-deletion paths formerly acquired a socket reference directly from conn->sk; the patch routes both through guarded acquisition.
Adds list-membership validation under the Bluetooth socket-list read lock.

negative_controls: No execution result for the reproducer on a particular build is included beyond the issue's recorded crash and patch test metadata.
Absence of this KASAN marker does not establish absence of all SCO lifetime races.
observability.positive_marker: A slab-use-after-free write in sco_sock_timeout during refcount/sock_hold processing.

preconditions: A kernel configuration/runtime capable of running the supplied syzkaller SCO reproducer, including its virtual-HCI setup.
An affected SCO implementation in which timeout work can wait while socket release unlinks and frees conn->sk.

sources.concept: Concurrent Bluetooth SCO socket lifecycle activity

impact.affected_asset: Freed Linux kernel Bluetooth SCO socket object.
impact.attacker_capability: Cause the supplied SCO lifecycle trigger to reach a KASAN-detected invalid refcount write; no further exploitation capability is established.
impact.security_effect: Kernel slab use-after-free write during socket reference-count acquisition.

causal_trace.summary: SCO socket creation and overlapping connect activity schedule a timeout/lifecycle scenario represented by the minimized syzkaller reproducer.

While sco_sock_timeout waits for sco_conn_lock, conn->sk can be unlinked and freed; the former path subsequently treated the connection field as eligible for reference acquisition without confirming list-based liveness.
The prior timeout-worker code assigned conn->sk and invoked sock_hold; the reported invalid access is a reference-count write through freed socket storage.
KASAN identifies a slab use-after-free write in sco_sock_timeout, and the free stack traces the object disposal through sco_sock_release.

failure.operation: sock_hold/refcount increment on conn->sk in sco_sock_timeout after the socket had been freed

primary_invariant.statement: A SCO timeout or connection-deletion path may call sock_hold on conn->sk only after establishing that the pointer still denotes a socket linked in sco_sk_list.
primary_invariant.violated_because: Waiting for sco_conn_lock allowed another path to unlink and free conn->sk before the worker used the saved pointer for sock_hold.

quality.review_notes: The issue provides a KASAN crash report, minimized C/Syz reproducers, and an upstream patch. The trigger is concurrency- and virtual-HCI/runtime-dependent, so repeatability is not asserted as deterministic. The bundle establishes a kernel UAF write only; it does not establish remote reachability, privilege gain, or code execution.

remediation.invariant_restored: The helper validates that conn->sk remains linked in sco_sk_list under the list read lock before calling sock_hold, otherwise returning no socket; timeout and connection-deletion paths use this guarded acquisition.

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The supplied reproducer creates an SCO socket and performs asynchronous then subsequent SCO connect operations with threaded execution and virtual HCI enabled.
data_structure_invariants: conn->sk must still name a socket linked in sco_sk_list before its reference count is incremented.
A socket unlinked and freed by the release path cannot be used as a reference-acquisition target.
state_context.state_machine: An SCO connection has timeout work pending; the timeout worker can wait on sco_conn_lock while a release path unlinks and frees the associated socket, after which the worker may resume.

target.component: Bluetooth SCO socket timeout and connection lifecycle

oracle.expected_negative: A build containing the guarded sco_sock_hold change should not emit that specific KASAN use-after-free write for the same reproducer.
oracle.expected_positive: The vulnerable build executing the supplied SCO lifecycle reproducer reports a slab use-after-free write in sco_sock_timeout during sock_hold/refcount increment.
